meta.adaptationwheel.world_border.hint: Approach the shared border. After stage four, walk toward it or choose Cross border. Access is personal and the outside area has a safe reach limit.
Exact repeats of safe system messages start adaptation. Player chat and danger warnings are never hidden. Stage four groups repeats into a counter.
A nearly full inventory starts adaptation. Stage one highlights duplicate stacks, stage two compacts compatible main-inventory stacks without deleting items. At stage four stacks in your inventory are no longer capped at 64: one slot holds any amount of one item (up to a billion). Tools, armour and potions still take one slot each; chests and other storage are unchanged.
meta.adaptationwheel.silent_world.hint: Mute Minecraft master volume. Real nearby sounds start adaptation; your own steps, swings and mount are ignored. Direction, captions and relative height unlock progressively; no entities are scanned outside sound events.
meta.adaptationwheel.memory_pressure.hin: Ten seconds of sustained high Java heap use starts adaptation. System.gc is never forced. At stage four the render distance drops by 2 chunks at a time (not below 6) while memory is short and returns after 30 calm seconds.
meta.adaptationwheel.low_tps.hint: Sustained slow server ticks start adaptation. Stage four batches wheel state persistence and service updates. It optimizes this mod, not every workload on the server.
meta.adaptationwheel.defeat_memory.hint: Death preserves recent combat events and a short movement trail. Stage one shows the trail near the death site. Stage four warns when a familiar dangerous combo prefix repeats. Dodge manually.
meta.adaptationwheel.pocket.returned: Items from the wheel pocket (%s) are back in your inventory: the pocket is replaced by unlimited stacks.
meta.adaptationwheel.pocket.returned_dro: Items from the wheel pocket (%s) are back; what did not fit lies at your feet. The pocket is replaced by unlimited stacks.

meta.adaptationwheel.foreign_mods.hint: The wheel remembers the mod list between launches. A changed pack starts adaptation. From stage one it names added and removed mods; at stage four it shows how many mobs and damage types each new mod brought and which mods were updated.
meta.adaptationwheel.foreign_mods.event: The pack changed: %s added, %s removed, %s updated.
meta.adaptationwheel.log_errors.hint: The wheel watches the game log. Thirty errors in a minute start adaptation. At stage four identical warnings and errors are trimmed: the first three copies and every 500th stay, the rest are not written. Fatal errors are never hidden.
meta.adaptationwheel.log_errors.event: Errors written to the log in the last minute: %s.
meta.adaptationwheel.log_errors.full: Repeated errors are trimmed, copies hidden so far: %s.

meta.adaptationwheel.world_rename.hint: The wheel leaves a marker in the world folder. If the world or its folder is renamed, the wheel recognises it and names its former name. At stage four it lists every former name and the date it met the world.
meta.adaptationwheel.world_rename.event: This world used to be called "%s", now "%s".
meta.adaptationwheel.world_rename.full: Former names: %s. The wheel has known this world since %s.
meta.adaptationwheel.config_edit.hint: Editing the wheel's config files while playing starts adaptation; settings apply immediately. At stage four the wheel shows exactly which values changed: old → new.
meta.adaptationwheel.clock_shift.hint: The wheel compares the computer clock with its own monotonic clock. Moving the clock by more than 30 seconds starts adaptation (computer sleep may count too). At stage four the wheel reports how much time really passed this session: its timers ignore clock changes.
meta.adaptationwheel.clock_shift.full: By the wheel's clock this session has lasted %s.
meta.adaptationwheel.crash_memory.hint: While you play the wheel keeps a marker and removes it on a normal exit. After a crash the next start begins adaptation and names the crash report. At stage four, rejoining the same world after a crash gives 30 seconds of protection from damage, fire and drowning.
meta.adaptationwheel.crash_memory.event: The last session in "%s" (%s) ended in a crash.
meta.adaptationwheel.crash_memory.other_: The crash happened in another world; no protection here.
meta.adaptationwheel.idle_player.hint: Three minutes without moving or turning the camera start adaptation. From stage one the wheel tells you how long you were away. At stage four, after a minute of idleness mobs lose you and cannot attack until you move. Environmental damage still applies.
meta.adaptationwheel.idle_player.shield: The wheel hides you from mobs while you stay still
meta.adaptationwheel.open_inventory.hint: Opening your inventory or a chest during combat starts adaptation. From stage two mob damage is halved while the menu is open; at stage four mobs cannot hurt you for the first 20 seconds after opening. Hitting a mob ends the protection.
meta.adaptationwheel.connection_loss.hin: The wheel checks the computer's network adapters and sends nothing anywhere. Losing the network starts adaptation; the wheel also reports when it is back. At stage four the online build analyses locally at once while the network is down.
meta.adaptationwheel.connection_loss.ful: The analyzer works locally without waiting for the network.
meta.adaptationwheel.wheel_update.hint: The wheel remembers its version between launches. Updating or downgrading the mod starts adaptation and the wheel names the old and new version. At stage four it tells you what changed.
meta.adaptationwheel.console_commands.hi: Cheat commands you type (/kill, /give, /gamemode, /effect, /tp and others) start adaptation. At stage four the wheel refuses /kill against you. Disable this adaptation in the J menu to allow /kill again.
meta.adaptationwheel.console_commands.re: The wheel refused /kill. Disable the "Console commands" adaptation in the J menu if you need it.

meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.17.0: New in 4.17.0: 11 adaptations to what happens outside the world: foreign mods, log errors, renamed worlds, config editing, clock changes, crashes, AFK, inventory in combat, network loss, wheel updates and cheat commands. Low memory now lowers the render distance.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.17.1: New in 4.17.1: World Slash is now a huge diagonal 64×20-block plane that cuts through walls and everything in its path, drawn as a black tear, 45 s cooldown (also cuts blocks). Fixed a possible crash when opening a world.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.17.2: New in 4.17.2: World Slash cuts blocks by default — it slices walls and ground along its plane (containers, unbreakable blocks, fluids and protected areas are spared). Can be turned off in the sword settings.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.18.0: New in 4.18.0: Pasha Boost 1.4 — after stage 4 of the low FPS adaptation the game runs much faster: shader lookup cache, particle light reuse, biome shortcut for ambient particles, culling of distant chests and signs, adaptive mob render distance. Test with OptiFine (400 mobs and 400 chests, signs and banners): 91 → 255 FPS. Turning it on no longer reloads resources.
gui.adaptationwheel.status.toggle: Click — turn this adaptation on or off
gui.adaptationwheel.detail.empty: Pick an adaptation in the list
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.20.0: New in 4.20.0: stage four of the overfull inventory adaptation no longer opens a 9-slot pocket; it lifts the stack limit instead, so one slot of your inventory holds any amount of one item. Big numbers in a slot are shortened (12k), the tooltip shows the exact count. Items from the old pocket return to your inventory by themselves.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.20.1: New in 4.20.1: World Slash deals 300 HP — 150 hearts — to every target through armour, resistance and absorption (was 150 HP).
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.21.0: New in 4.21.0: Pasha Boost is now called Adapt Boost (1.6); your settings are kept. Memory savings from FerriteCore: block states share tables, equal block models and shapes are stored once — about 1.1 GB less memory in a 23-mod pack. Active from the next launch after Boost is unlocked. Also: particles are turned once per frame, experience orbs of the same value merge (fewer entities on farms), the game draws at most 30 frames per second in the background and 10 when minimised.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.21.1: Fixed in 4.21.1: the game no longer crashes on death or when the wheel comes off with Fabulous graphics (Adapt Boost restored it without its buffers), nor on water splashes, rain and drips with OptiFine (a particle dropped over the limit broke the water recolouring).
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.22.0: New in 4.22.0: the analyzer classifies attacks more precisely. Untagged vanilla damage (bee stings, thorns, cactus, suffocating in a wall) is recognised exactly; a bee sting is no longer a projectile. Mod tags such as forge:magic and forge:curse are read, so Jujutsu Craft curse hits and other mod damage get their category. Jujutsu techniques and conditions from compatibility tables show as known instead of a 30% guess. The name vocabulary was extended from 24 mods: hypothermia is cold, plague and infection are poison, gorgon is magic, swords and whips are physical.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.23.0: New in 4.23.0: a reworked adaptation menu. A wide window shows the list and the details side by side: the selected row's details open on the right. A short window gets a compact header and more rows. Keyboard: arrows select, Enter opens details, Space turns an adaptation on or off, typing goes straight to the search (except the menu key itself; use Ctrl+F for it), Esc clears it. The category picker shows how many adaptations each category has. In the details the analysis starts with the category and confidence, explanations are fainter than the main lines. The corner panel shows the protection a stage leads to instead of the current 0%. The menu is no longer see-through.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.19.0: New in 4.19.0: the Sword of Extermination is worn on the forearm like Mahoraga's, and parrying raises the arm into a guard. New adaptation menu (J): a compact list with stages, protection and progress, a category picker, a stage timeline in the details and a refreshed corner panel. Pasha Boost 1.5: a new screen with a frame-time graph and savings per second, honest settings, distant mobs update less often on the client and particles stop producing garbage.
meta.adaptationwheel.near_misses.hint: Miss a visible mob with your arrow or supported bullet within two blocks. Stage IV guides projectiles toward a target within 64 blocks: your aimed target first, then a nearby enemy. Native damage, shields and collisions remain in effect; this adaptation does not pierce walls.

skin.adaptationwheel.classic.tagline: The familiar look: rim, eight spokes and ornaments.
skin.adaptationwheel.classic.description: The wheel it all started with: a faceted golden rim, eight spokes and nine stepped ornaments. Every stage turns it by 45 degrees; while adapting to existence it spins without stopping.
skin.adaptationwheel.clockwork.tagline: Every stage is one more click of the mechanism.
skin.adaptationwheel.clockwork.descripti: A brass gear with sixteen teeth and sapphire marks on its rim. Above it a steel wheel with its own teeth turns the other way, and on the still axle in the centre two hands move: the hour hand steps with the wheel, the minute hand goes round once a minute. An open clockwork above your head.
skin.adaptationwheel.ice_crown.tagline: Spikes of ice grow above your head.
skin.adaptationwheel.ice_crown.descripti: The crown hangs lower and closer to the head than the other wheels: a silver band with eight tall ice spikes and eight short ones between them. The ice darkens towards the base and glows at the tips; sixteen icicles hang under the band. Inside the crown a glowing snowflake turns slowly, with four ice shards floating around it.
skin.adaptationwheel.armillary.tagline: Every celestial ring turns above you.
skin.adaptationwheel.armillary.descripti: A golden armillary sphere on a still axle. Half the segments of every ring are another colour, and the stripes run round, so each ring is seen turning. The rim with eight blue signs goes one way, the large vertical ring the other, the small vertical ring the first way again, and the tilted ecliptic ring with three glowing planets against it. The star in the centre spins fastest. The sphere hangs higher than the other wheels so it does not touch the head.
skin.adaptationwheel.event_horizon.tagli: A black hole circles above you.
skin.adaptationwheel.event_horizon.descr: A small black hole above the head: a black sphere with a thin ring of light around it and a slightly tilted disc of three belts — white, orange and violet. The inner belts turn faster than the outer ones, so their stripes wind into a spiral. Rock fragments drift slowly beyond the disc's edge.
skin.adaptationwheel.ouroboros.tagline: A serpent holds its own tail — a circle without end.
skin.adaptationwheel.ouroboros.descripti: An emerald serpent coiled into a ring holds its tail in its mouth. Its scales run in bands of dark and light emerald, golden diamonds and bone spikes line its back. A golden crest on its head, glowing yellow eyes and horns curving back. Golden scales float inside the ring, and a glowing emerald hovers in the centre.
skin.adaptationwheel.storm_ring.descript: A ring of dark clouds above the head: rain falls from under them, four lightning bolts strike along the edge and blue sparks flicker on the cloud tops. In the middle is the eye of the storm: a glowing core with a vortex, and wind circling around it.
skin.adaptationwheel.malevolent_shrine.t: A shrine above your head, blades cutting around it in waves.
skin.adaptationwheel.malevolent_shrine.d: Sukuna's shrine stands above your head: a dark temple with two black roofs, bull horns and a fanged maw on its front, on a mound of skulls in a pool of blood. There is no barrier — an open domain: cuts flash in waves around the shrine. Each is a bent blade with sharp ends: it flies out white-hot, cools to red and is gone, and the long ones cross each other. On everything around you the cuts land in fans: chips fly from blocks and smouldering marks stay, red drops fly from mobs. Picture only: blocks stay whole, nothing takes damage.
skin.adaptationwheel.infinite_void.descr: Gojo Satoru's domain above your head: a black sphere of void sparkling with stars, a blue sphere of Infinity and six bright eyes around it. Further out three tilted streams of endless information circle — red, blue and violet — while Blue and Red float at the edges among distant stars.

meta.adaptationwheel.broken_tool.hint: An item of yours breaking (a tool, weapon, armour piece or shield) starts adaptation. At stage one the wheel warns you on the action bar when an item in your hands or on your body is down to 10% durability. At stage two a breaking item is restored to 25% durability instead, at stage three to 50%, at stage four completely. An elytra worn down to 1 durability is restored the same way. Take the wheel off or switch this entry off to make items break as usual.
meta.adaptationwheel.broken_tool.saved: %s was about to break and is restored to %s%% durability
meta.adaptationwheel.too_expensive.hint: An anvil refusing with "Too Expensive!" (a price of 40 levels or more) starts adaptation. At stage one the screen shows the real price instead of that label. From stage two your limit grows: 50 levels, at stage three 60, at stage four there is no limit. You still pay the full price in levels.
meta.adaptationwheel.empty_quiver.hint: Trying to draw a bow without arrows starts adaptation. At stage one, while you carry fewer than 8 arrows, the wheel tells you how many are left. At stage two the bow can be drawn with no arrows and shoots at half power, costing 3 durability; at stage three at full power for 2 durability; at stage four at full power for 1. Such arrows cannot be picked up; Power, Punch and Flame work as usual. Crossbows are not affected.
meta.adaptationwheel.item_cooldown.hint: Trying to use an item that is still recharging (ender pearl, chorus fruit, a shield after an axe, goat horn and other Minecraft items) starts adaptation. For you these cooldowns are 15% shorter at stage one, 30% at stage two, 40% at stage three and 50% at stage four. Items from other mods are not affected.
meta.adaptationwheel.enderman_gaze.hint: An enderman that gets angry because you looked at it starts this adaptation. At stage I endermen farther than 48 blocks no longer take your look as a challenge, at stage II farther than 24, at stage III farther than 8, and at stage IV your gaze never angers them. An enderman you hit or angered some other way stays angry.
meta.adaptationwheel.creeper_grief.hint: A creeper explosion that breaks blocks within 16 blocks of you starts this adaptation. At stages I to IV, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % of the blocks the blast would have broken survive (the highest stage among nearby wheel wearers counts). Damage to creatures is unchanged.
meta.adaptationwheel.piglin_gold.hint: A piglin that attacks you because you wear no gold starts this adaptation. At stages I to III the wheel warns you above the hotbar; at IV piglins treat you as if you wore gold and do not attack on sight. Piglin brutes stay hostile, and piglins still get angry if you hit one or open a chest near them.
meta.adaptationwheel.piglin_gold.angry: Piglins are angry: you wear no gold
meta.adaptationwheel.villager_trade.hint: Opening trades with a villager or wandering trader where a price has risen from demand or a trade is sold out starts this adaptation. The demand surcharge in your trades is 25 % lower (I), 50 % lower (II) and gone (III). At IV the wheel also restocks sold-out trades, at most once a minute per merchant.
meta.adaptationwheel.surrounded.hint: When four or more hostile mobs within 8 blocks target you, this adaptation starts. When you hit a mob in melee, other hostile mobs targeting you take part of the blow: 25 % within 1.5 blocks (I), 50 % and 2 blocks (II), 75 % and 2.5 blocks (III), 100 % and 3 blocks (IV). Tamed and peaceful creatures are not affected.
meta.adaptationwheel.sticky_blocks.hint: Being slowed by a cobweb, powder snow, a sweet berry bush, soul sand without Soul Speed or a honey block starts adaptation. Each stage cuts the slowdown by a quarter: 25%, 50%, 75%, and at stage four these blocks no longer hold you back (honey's jump penalty too). Berry and freezing damage stay. Switch it off in the J menu to get vanilla movement back at once.
meta.adaptationwheel.portal_wait.hint: Standing inside a nether portal starts adaptation. The wait before the portal takes you drops from 4 seconds to 3 at stage one, 2 at stage two, 1 at stage three and to a single tick at stage four. Creative mode is unaffected.
meta.adaptationwheel.loose_footing.hint: Digging a block while swimming without Aqua Affinity or while off the ground starts adaptation. Vanilla slows each of these to a fifth; each stage lifts it a fifth more, so at stage four mining in the air or under water is as fast as on dry land.
meta.adaptationwheel.trampled_farmland.h: Trampling farmland by jumping or falling on it, on foot or on a mount you ride, starts adaptation. From stage one the soil survives with a chance of 25%, 50%, 75%, and at stage four it never turns to dirt under you.
meta.adaptationwheel.smelting_wait.hint: Watching a working furnace, smoker, blast furnace or brewing stand with its menu open starts adaptation. After that every vanilla furnace and brewing stand within 8 blocks of you works faster: 1.25x, 1.5x, 2x and 3x at stages one to four, burning fuel at the same rate. Taking the wheel off or switching the adaptation off stops it at once.
meta.adaptationwheel.nether_water.hint: Pouring a water bucket in the Nether, where it evaporates, starts adaptation. The water then stays for 3 seconds at stage one, 10 at stage two, 30 at stage three, and at stage four it stays for good. The source is removed with a hiss when its time is up.
meta.adaptationwheel.day_sleep.hint: Trying to lie down in a bed of a normal dimension while it is too early to sleep starts adaptation. At stage one the wheel tells you how long is left until you can sleep. At stage two you can lie down by day: your spawn point is set and the rest timer resets, but the time of day does not change. At stage three sleeping by day skips to the evening. At stage four, sneaking while you click the bed sends you to the next morning instead. When several players sleep, vanilla's rule about enough sleepers stays and the highest stage among the sleepers decides.
meta.adaptationwheel.day_sleep.frozen: Time is not passing, so evening will never come
meta.adaptationwheel.restless_sleep.hint: A bed that refuses you because of monsters nearby starts adaptation. At stage one the monsters that stop you sleeping glow for five seconds. At stage two only monsters within 5 blocks of you count, at stage three only those within 3 blocks. At stage four monsters never stop you from sleeping. Monsters with their own rule, such as angry zombified piglins, keep it. Damage still wakes you.
meta.adaptationwheel.insomnia.hint: Every night when phantoms look for a player who has not slept for three days or more, adaptation starts. At stage one the wheel tells you how many nights you have gone without sleep. At stage two phantoms come for you only after 4 days without rest, at stage three after 5 days, and at stage four never. Sleeping in a bed resets the counter as usual.
meta.adaptationwheel.foreign_bed.hint: Clicking a bed in the Nether or the End, where it explodes, starts adaptation. At stage one the first click only warns you and the bed explodes if you click again within 5 seconds. At stage two the bed disappears in a blast that damages nothing but those standing next to it. At stage three the bed does not explode; it just does not let you sleep. At stage four clicking the bed makes it your personal respawn point: after death the wheel brings you back next to it while it stands, and an ordinary spawn point set later replaces it.

meta.adaptationwheel.foreign_bed.anchor_: The wheel remembered this bed as your respawn point
The bed the wheel remembered is gone

meta.adaptationwheel.murky_water.hint: Having your eyes under water starts this adaptation. Underwater fog then reaches farther than in vanilla: 25 percent farther at stage I, 50 percent at stage II, twice as far at stage III and three times as far at stage IV (never past your render distance). Only you see it, and only the ordinary water fog changes; blindness and darkness keep their own fog.
meta.adaptationwheel.lava_sight.hint: Having your eyes in lava while it cannot hurt you (Fire Resistance, or the wheel fully adapted to both lava and burning) starts this adaptation. Instead of the thick vanilla fog you see through lava up to 5 blocks at stage I, 8 at stage II, 12 at stage III and 20 at stage IV. Only you see it; lava still burns everyone who is not protected.
meta.adaptationwheel.unseen_foes.hint: Being hurt by an invisible mob starts this adaptation. Invisible mobs near you are then drawn with a glowing outline: within 4 blocks at stage I, 8 at stage II, 16 at stage III and 32 at stage IV. Players and armor stands are never outlined, and only you see it. Needs entity outlines to be drawn (some shader packs turn them off).
meta.adaptationwheel.laptop_battery.hint: Playing on a laptop that runs on its battery starts this adaptation (a desktop without a battery never does; the wheel reads the power state in the background every 10 seconds). Stage I shows the charge in the top-left corner, stage II limits the frame rate to 60, stage III to 45 and lowers the render distance by 2 chunks, stage IV to 30 and by 4 chunks (never below 6). Plugging in, taking the wheel off or turning the adaptation off gives your own settings back; anything you change yourself is left alone.
meta.adaptationwheel.dry_riptide.hint: A Riptide trident does nothing on dry land without rain, and every such try starts this adaptation. At stage I the wheel tells you what is missing. At stage II snowfall counts as rain, and the trident stays wet for 5 more seconds after water or rain. At stage III the dash works anywhere, at half power on dry land. At stage IV anywhere, at 75% power on dry land (adjustable in the settings from 50 to 100%). The trident wears down as usual.
meta.adaptationwheel.dry_riptide.dried: The trident has dried: Riptide needs water, rain or snow
meta.adaptationwheel.shattered_eye.hint: An Eye of Ender that shatters after a throw starts this adaptation. At stage I, after a throw, the wheel tells you how many blocks away the stronghold is. At stage II eyes shatter half as often: 1 in 10 instead of 1 in 5. At stage III they never shatter. At stage IV they never shatter and come back to your hand by themselves (or to the inventory if your hand is busy) when you are within 64 blocks of where they came down.
meta.adaptationwheel.shattered_eye.retur: The Eye of Ender came back
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.29.0: 23 new utility adaptations: day sleep, sleeping near monsters, insomnia, beds in other dimensions, sticky blocks, portals, mining while floating, farmland, furnaces, water in the Nether, broken tools are restored, anvil limit, bow without arrows, item cooldowns, endermen, creepers, piglins, villager prices, crowds, murky water, lava sight, invisible mobs and laptop battery

meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.32.0: Advancements: the wheel has its own tab — the wheel obtained and worn, the first adaptation, the first stage IV, stage V (existence), the first menu opening, plus the Sword of Extermination and the World Slash. meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.33.3: Armillary Sphere: each ring is seen turning — half the segments of every ring are another colour, and all rings turn faster, the rim once in 24 seconds. Shape and size are unchanged. The other looks, stages, protection and sounds are unchanged
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.34.0: Clearer interface: the J menu label says Working, Off or Not worn, the list is split into groups, categories have icons, the details open with a Now card and a What it gives section, times are real (speed-up included), the HUD sits under the effect icons and lights a stage just reached, chat names the stage, and the wheel and sword tooltips are shorter. meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.35.0: Clear learning modes: the Analyzer learning window shows three cards side by side — Base only, Learns in combat and Combat + world study — with the same ✓/✗ list, the load and when to pick each; a line on top says protection and stages are earned the same way in every mode, and the bottom says what a mode change keeps. meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.37.0: Wheel summary in the J menu: the list starts with «Wheel summary» and the menu opens on it (Home returns to it). On the right: the wheel with a mark per adaptation, «What's next», running / waiting / off counters (a click leaves one group in the list), a tip, protection by category with weak spots and a «Recent» feed of this game. Waiting rows say «hit → stage 2 · 40%», the adaptation that ends before the others says «ends first», and the details have a «History» section. In a narrow window Enter opens the summary as its own screen
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.38.0: New wheel look «Malevolent Shrine»: Sukuna's shrine on a mound of skulls in a pool of blood. Cuts flash and fade around the shrine: each sweeps out, holds for a split second and is gone, and the next one flashes somewhere else. The cuts also land on everything around — blocks, mobs, animals and other players within 10 blocks; twice as many while adapting to existence. Picture only: blocks stay whole, nothing takes damage. Pick it in the «Wheel look» menu (Ctrl+K); the cuts around turn off with the «Cuts around (Malevolent Shrine)» setting in Configured
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.39.0: New wheel look «Infinite Void»: Gojo Satoru's domain — a black void sphere with stars, the blue sphere of Infinity, six eyes, three information streams, Blue and Red. Pick it in the wheel look menu; the look does not affect combat or the world.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.40.0: The tagline and description of the «Infinite Void» look are now hidden by flickering noise: the «Adapt to the text» button in the wheel look menu starts a one-stage, 20-second adaptation that runs while this look is open. The white stream around the sphere is now red. Fixed the broken letters in the look's strings and in the 4.39.0 update text.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.41.0: The cuts of the «Malevolent Shrine» look got better. Instead of straight sticks there are bent blades with sharp ends and soft light: they come in waves, and the long ones cross each other. On blocks the cuts land in fans, chips of the block's colour fly and smouldering marks stay; on mobs, red drops. Still picture only: blocks stay whole, nothing takes damage.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.44.0: You can correct a category by hand. If the analyzer is wrong or unsure, open «Details for configuration» in the J menu and press «Correct…» or K: a window shows all 14 categories. Only the category name and the stage times of that row change, and a running stage keeps its percentage. Protection, stages and other rows stay as they are, the analyzer keeps gathering data, and «Back to the analyzer» removes the correction.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.45.2: Malevolent Shrine cuts and the look's blade light now show correctly with OptiFine shader packs: no black streaks (LUMA) and no screen-wide white blob (Chocapic), no stray coloured streaks towards the sky (Builders). Without shaders nothing changes.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.46.0: The Infinite Void look changes the world around it: a flickering stream of glyphs runs over mobs near the wheel, after 8 seconds a mob trembles and symbols drip down it; star dust circles and falls into the black core; a blue ring closes in on the feet while a red one spreads out. All of it is picture only, and each part can be switched off in the look's settings.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.47.0: The Learning screen now explains what definitions are in a line under their count; hover the «?» for details: which damage types and effects count, how fast the analyzer reads them and when new ones appear.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.48.0: Times in the menu and HUD are now in seconds of adaptation, at speed ×1: another hit does not change the numbers, it makes the countdown run faster. The speed shows as a gold «×1.30» badge, and after a hit the row briefly shows «+30% speed». Element experience no longer shortens stages; it gives speed from their start: +5% per mastered source, up to +35%.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.48.1: MIT licence and updated third-party notices inside the jar. No gameplay changes.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.49.0: Distant Horizons is no longer bundled, and the Landscape memory adaptation and its two settings are gone with it; stage IV of Memory pressure now only lowers the render distance. The Infinite Void look no longer draws the blue and red rings at the wearer's feet, and their setting is gone; the stream of glyphs over mobs and the star dust stay.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.45.1: Protection against damage that bypasses the wheel was checked in seven mods (Hex Casting, Goety, Mana and Artifice, Enigmatic Legacy, Re-Avaritia, Goety: Revelation, Simply Swords): all their direct health writes already go through the wheel. The health price of the Simply Swords Ward ability is no longer treated as an attack, like the Blood Magic dagger.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.45.0: Wider mod compatibility: about 430 damage types from 616 mods get their category from a compatibility table, the analyzer knows new words (minigun, railgun, rot, swarm…), 5 more harmful effects and 134 mobs from 49 mods get a known category. In the J menu a «Knowledge from» row shows that the table decided the category and which mod it came from. Earned stages and your corrections stay as they are.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.43.0: The analyzer is more accurate. One hit starts one adaptation: a mod arrow no longer adds a stray «Arrow» row, and a mod creature's plain bite no longer adds a second row. Anonymous damage is split by mod. Mod zombies are no longer treated as the plain zombie, and flying abilities with a lot of health no longer count as bosses. Learning memory loses only what really changed, not everything on each update. Danger is measured by damage pace over 5 seconds. New: element experience, each mastered source of a category makes new ones 5% faster, up to 35%, and protection never carries over. The new /adaptation why command shows why the analyzer decided what it did.
meta.adaptationwheel.changelog.4.42.0: The analyzer no longer mixes up adaptations. A blast from a ghast, a creeper or anyone else now teaches «Explosions», not a separate «Player explosions», and the stage you earned moves there. A creature's row shows its main attack instead of jumping with every hit. A guardian's beam and evoker fangs are now «Indirect magic», not «Instant Damage». The analyzer's memory limits are gone: nothing learned gets pushed out.
